title: Artificial intelligence in higher education: the state of the field
explain_beginner: This paper reviewed 138 studies about artificial intelligence in higher education from 2016 to 2022. It found that publications grew very quickly in 2021 and 2022, rising two to three times above earlier years. Research happened on six continents, and China replaced the US as the leader. Education departments became the main source of researchers. Most studies focused on undergraduate students and on language learning. AI was mostly used for assessment, prediction, tutoring, helping as an assistant, and managing student learning. The review also points to gaps, including newer tools like ChatGPT, showing where future research could go.
explain_business: This review of 138 studies shows AI in higher education is expanding fast, especially in 2021 and 2022, with China now leading research output. Most work targets undergraduate students and language learning, and the main uses are assessment, prediction, tutoring, AI assistance, and managing learning. For executives, this signals where adoption and investment are concentrating, and it highlights that instructors and managers are studied far less than students. The identified gaps, including newer tools such as ChatGPT, suggest areas where current evidence is thin, which can inform planning, procurement, and research priorities.
explain_practitioner: This systematic review followed PRISMA principles and protocol, identifying 138 articles from 2016 to 2022 for full examination. Data were extracted and coded using a priori and grounded coding. Publications rose nearly two to three times in 2021 and 2022 compared with prior years. Research spanned six continents, with leadership shifting from the US to China, and education departments becoming the dominant researcher affiliation. Undergraduates were the most studied group at 72 percent, and language learning was the most common subject. Five usage codes emerged: assessment or evaluation, predicting, AI assistant, intelligent tutoring system, and managing student learning.
